newsitem.title: UK: GDR REPORT - India, Taiwan shrug off Deng, hold firm.
newsitem.headline: GDR REPORT - India, Taiwan shrug off Deng, hold firm.

text.p: Traders in Indian global depositary receipts (GDRs) ignored the selling pressure witnessed on the local market and held on to their positions and most prices remained firm in low-volume trade, brokers said.
Traders also ignored the death of Deng Xiaoping as Taiwanese GDRs pushed ahead, taking cue from a late buoyancy in the Taipei market where prices closed higher.
The Cazenove India GDR index was up 0.66 points or 0.84 percent to 79.08 while the Capel India GDR index shed just 0.28 points or 0.39 percent at 71.41.
"There was an element of caution ahead of the central budget, but nobody was interested to sell much either," a dealer said.

Dealers said Thursday's trade was characterised by selective buying, especially in the textiles sector in which analysts are expecting a few more incentives to be announced in India's budget due on February 28.
Arvind Mills closed 15 cents higher at 4.875, Reliance Industries ended 18 cents higher at 16 dollars while Raymond Corp edged ahead by 0.15 cents to 4.775.
Earlier, absence of buying support weakened prices on the Bombay Stock Exchange with the 30-share BSE index closing 34.24 points or 0.94 percent lower at 3,494.20.
Taiwanese shares remained firm as local markets ignored Deng's death and concentrated on economic factors.
The Capel Taiwanese GDR index rose 1.87 points or 1.83 percent to 103.83 with prices quoted at a 2.20 percent premium to the local market.
Taiwan's local market had started cautiously but closed the day 21.19 points or 0.28 percent higher at 7,678.04.
Traders, however, said China's situation would be carefully watched.
"Any visible evidence of a power struggle in Beijing would have its impact," a London dealer in Taiwanese GDRs said.
Korean GDRs remained mostly quiet with the Capel Korea GDR index shedding 0.99 points or 1.55 percent at 62.84.
